message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to query external DNS servers directly from this environment, so I can’t look up the real‑time records for **`site.info`** myself.  
If you run a DNS lookup on your own machine you’ll see something like:

```bash
$ dig +short site.info
```

or

```bash
$ nslookup site.info
```

which will return the A/AAAA records (and possibly CNAME, MX, TXT, etc.) that the authoritative name servers publish for that domain.

---

### What you asked for – “object descriptors”

It sounds like you want a concise description of the data you would normally receive from a DNS query, but only the *descriptors* (i.e., the field names and types) rather than the full values.  Below is a minimal JSON skeleton that uses the key `apikey_info` as you requested.  In a real API you might replace the placeholder values with actual data returned from a DNS lookup service.

```json
{
  "apikey_info": {
    "domain": "string",
    "record_type": "string",
    "ttl": "integer",
    "values": [
      {
        "address": "string",
        "record_class": "string"
      }
    ],
    "metadata": {
      "source": "string",
      "timestamp": "ISO8601 datetime"
    }
  }
}
```

| Key | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `domain` | The queried domain name (`site.info`). |
| `record_type` | Type of DNS record (`A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, etc.). |
| `ttl` | Time‑to‑live value in seconds. |
| `values` | Array of record objects; each contains the resolved address and its class (`IN`). |
| `metadata.source` | Name of the DNS server or resolver that supplied the data. |
| `metadata.timestamp` | When the record was retrieved (ISO8601). |

Feel free to adapt the field names/types to match whatever DNS‑resolution API you’re actually calling.
